entry.title: Bypassing Administrator Protection by Abusing UI Access. A headline feature introduced in the latest release of Windows 11, 25H2 is Administrator Protection.
entry.summary:
A headline feature introduced in the latest release of Windows 11, 25H2 is Administrator Protection. The goal of this feature is to replace User Account Control (UAC) with a more robust and importantly, securable system to allow a local user to access administrator privileges only when necessary. This blog post will give a brief overview of the new feature, how it works and how it’s different from UAC.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os

entry.title: Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization for Bounded-Payoff Imperfect-Information Games
entry.summary:
Imperfect-information games with a graded-reward structure present significant computational challenges for equilibrium computation, since the payoff expectations must be estimated across exponentially large strategy spaces. Counterfactual Regret Minimization over the years has proven effective for approximating Nash equilibria, but Monte Carlo variants create a large overhead of sampling costs when the counterfactual values are estimated from sampled game-tree trajectories. We propose a novel Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization, a framework that uses Quantum Amplitude Estimation to reduce the computational complexity of the regret updates in bounded-payoff imperfect-information games, while preserving the convergence of its classical counterpart.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #decision-theory #infosec

entry.title: More Keys, Less Commitment: Key-Committing Attacks on BBB Accordions via Encode-then-Encipher and a Key-Committing Transform
entry.summary:
Cryptographic accordions with beyond-birthday-bound (BBB) security are being actively studied in connection with NIST’s ongoing standardization effort. We show that BBB security of an accordion does not necessarily strengthen key commitment of AE built from it: in many BBB accordions, additional keys introduced for BBB security give an adversary extra degrees of freedom. Exploiting this observation, we present $O(1)$ key-committing attacks on a broad range of AE schemes built from BBB accordions, mostly via the Encode-then-Encipher (EtE) paradigm, including CHCTR2, eCTR-based accordions, THCTR, HCTR+, TCT2, and bbb-ddd-AES under a natural polynomial-hash instantiation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics #infosec

entry.title: PERSEPHONE: Zero-Knowledge Multiplicative Non-Negative Proof for Sequential Private Range Verification
entry.summary:
Privacy is a fundamental requirement of modern digital payment systems, which process highly sensitive financial data, including account balances and transaction amounts. Unauthorized disclosure of this information can compromise users’ financial privacy and expose them to fraud or other forms of financial abuse. A key challenge in this setting is to verify that a payment amount does not exceed the payer’s available balance without revealing either the payment amount or the balance.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: Debiasing Law Enforcement Officers: Evidence from an Expressive Arts Intervention in India -- by Sofia Amaral, Girija Borker, Nishith Prakash, María Micaela Sviatschi
entry.summary:
Frontline state agents exercise substantial discretion over citizens’ access to public services, yet little is known about whether the attitudes and beliefs shaping this discretion can be changed among incumbent bureaucrats. Partnering with the Bihar Police - one of India’s largest states that operates under comparatively severe policing capacity constraints, we conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial across 417 police stations and roughly 2,500 active duty senior field police officers to evaluate a three-day expressive arts intervention, grounded in the Theatre of the Oppressed, designed to change police responses to gender-based violence (GBV). Approximately 7 months after baseline, treated officers exhibit more favorable attitudes toward GBV, greater empathy, and stronger legal knowledge.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #infosec #agents
